published_statement: IAU 2015 B3 (arXiv:1510.07674) Recommends 3: '1(GM)^N_sun = 1.327 124 4 x 10^20 m^3 s^-2', nominal values 'by definition exact ... conversion factors only ... not as the true solar properties' (Rec. 1); Rec. 5: 'if SI masses are explicitly needed, they should be expressed in terms of (GM)_object/G, where the estimate of the Newtonian constant G should be specified in the publication (for example, the 2014 CODATA value is G = 6.67408 (+-0.00031) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2)'; Noting 3: 'G is currently one of the least precisely determined constants, whereas the error in the product GM_sun is five orders of magnitude smaller'. Prsa et al. 2016 App. A (arXiv:1605.09788): G_2006 'yields a nominal solar mass of M^N_sun = 1.988416 x 10^30 kg'; G_2014 'yields a solar mass of M_sun = (1.988475 +- 0.000092) x 10^30 kg'. CODATA 2022 (arXiv:2409.03787) Table XXXII: 'speed of light in vacuum c 299 792 458 m s^-1 exact'; 'Newtonian constant of gravitation G 6.674 30(15) x 10^-11 m^3 kg^-1 s^-2 2.2 x 10^-5'; Sec. I.B.11: 'the 2022 and 2018 recommended values of G are therefore identical'. No source read here prints 1.98892e30 kg; no IAU resolution defines a solar mass in kilograms.
published_hypotheses: B3-H1: only the mass PARAMETER (GM)^N_sun is nominal and exact; a solar mass in kg is not a nominal constant (Rec. 1, 3)

B3-H3: G is the limiting uncertainty; GM_sun is known ~1e5 times better (Noting 3)
CODATA-H1: G's recommended uncertainty carries a 3.9 expansion factor because the 16 inputs are mutually inconsistent (Sec. I.B.11, XV.A)

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. The 1.98892e30 figure is, by numerical match, GM_sun/G with CODATA 1986's G = 6.67259e-11 -- a value computed when G was known to 1.3e-4 (the (85) in 6.672 59(85) is NAMED-NOT-READ). What came later: CODATA 2006/2014/2018/2022 moved G up by +2.57e-4 to 6.67430e-11, and IAU 2015 B3 made GM_sun (not M_sun) the exact conversion constant precisely because G is the weak datum (Noting 3). So the authors of 1.98892e30 DID lack later G data, and having it DOES change the number (1.98892 -> 1.98841 e30, 11.4 sigma of today's CODATA G). Evidence the other way: (a) G is still contested -- CODATA needs a 3.9 expansion factor and Rinaldi et al. 2022 argue for u(G) ~ 2.2e-4, under which the old value is 0.94 sigma away; the 16 inputs span 5.5e-4 and contain the implied G; (b) every conclusion phase1 draws is G-free in solar-mass units or printed at 3 figures: 14.7 km, 2.57e10, 1.28e12, 1.349e26 and Theorem 4's 3/2 are all unchanged by the updated data (computed). The light year and the year are definitions, not data, and nobody lacked anything there; the tree's ly is only truncated. Conclusion: the datum moved, the conclusions did not.
grade_evidence: Computed (sympy, exact rationals, exit 0). The year STANDS (exact). The light year STANDS as a 5-figure truncation (-3.2e-6). The solar mass as written does NOT reproduce from current sources at the precision written: B3 Rec. 5 requires G x M_sun = (GM)^N_sun, and with the tree's own G (phase1.py:212, CODATA 2018 = 2022, READ) the tree's 1.98892e30 violates it by +2.5655e-4 = 11.42 sigma of G; the consistent value is 1.98841e30. That is a hypothesis of the source dropped at phase1.py:212-213, so the result holds on a smaller class than the tree writes: to <= 3.6 significant figures, which covers every figure phase1 PRINTS and every verdict it draws (14.7 km, 2.57e10 and 1.28e12 solar masses, 1.349e26 kg/m, Theorem 4's exact 3/2), but not the 5-6 figures the constants carry nor the selftest pins. Not WRONG: nothing refutes any conclusion, the offset is inside the G-input span and within 1 sigma of a published conservative G (arXiv:2209.07416), and B3 itself concedes G is the limiting datum. Not DATA-DEPENDENT for the conclusions: no printed conclusion moves. Recorded discrepancies, not repaired and not refutations: pins 1.4742e4 (phase1.py:506, function returns 1.47442e4) and 6.3113e7 / 6.3113e4 (phase1.py:473, 481; function returns 6.31150e7) differ from the owner's own computed values in the 4th-5th figure and pass only under rtol 1e-3; 1.98892e30 recurs in ~20 other modules (kerr, navigate, shipspec, launcher, drivespec, gate, wormhole, ...), out of scope here and not graded. Caveat on the read: alphaXiv quota was exhausted, so sources were READ from full-text copies harvested earlier in this workflow; the Julian-year/light-year definitions and CODATA 1986 are NAMED-NOT-READ.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: phase1.py pairing SOLAR_MASS with its G so G x M_sun = (GM)^N_sun (1.98841e30 for CODATA 2018/2022), or a restatement of the constants at the <= 3-4 figure precision the conclusions use -- the owner's call, not this audit's. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a G measurement or CODATA adjustment moving G by >~1e-3 (enough to change a printed third figure of a kg-denominated figure such as 1.349e26), which nothing in the 16 inputs or the 2022 literature read here indicates. To WRONG: only a computed change of a phase1 verdict, and the re-derivation shows none is possible from these constants (Theorem 4 is constant-free; the price figures are linear in GM_sun).
